key_insight: Per-query selection of retrieval-agent configurations (LLM, retriever, docs, hops, synthesis) lets you meet an accuracy or budget target while substantially reducing cost compared to one-size-fits-all pipelines.
problem_solved: Retrieval pipelines are typically hand-tuned per workload, leaving per-query cost/accuracy trade-offs untapped — the paper automates choosing the best configuration for each query given an accuracy or budget constraint.
method: Formulate configuration selection as a per-query decision problem: given a natural-language query and a target (accuracy or budget), choose from a catalog of predefined pipeline configurations.

Estimate or learn the cost/accuracy trade-offs of catalog entries and use a lightweight selector to pick the configuration that satisfies the target while minimizing cost (or maximizing accuracy under budget).
Evaluate per-query selection against static baselines to show reduced serving cost and preserved or improved answer quality.
impact: Enables dynamic, query-level tuning of retrieval agents to cut serving costs and improve resource allocation without sacrificing accuracy — practical for production RAG systems and MLops teams.
visual_elements: Flow diagram: Query → Selector → Chosen Configuration (LLM, retriever, docs, hops, synthesis) → Retrieval + Answer
Cost vs. Accuracy trade-off plot showing static vs per-query selection curves and cost savings area
Bar chart or table comparing average cost and accuracy for static baseline vs per-query optimized pipeline
Icon grid of configuration knobs (model, retriever, docs, hops, synthesis) to illustrate the search space
paper_title: Natural Language Query to Configuration for Retrieval Agents
paper_authors: Melissa Z. Pan, Negar Arabzadeh, Mathew Jacob, Fiodar Kazhamiaka, Esha Choukse
